dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:7601.text: A fish's name, found in 潘 country in 樂浪. Formed from 魚, with 虜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7602.text: A fish's name. It resembles a shrimp, without feet, one cun long and as thick as a fork's prong, and occurs in 遼東. Formed from 魚, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7603.text: A fish's name, found in 潘 country in 樂浪. Formed from 魚, with 妾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7604.text: A fish's name, found in 潘 country in 樂浪. Formed from 魚, with 巿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7605.text: A fish's name, found in 潘 country in 樂浪. Formed from 魚, with 匊 indicating the sound. Alternatively, the 䱡 fish occurs east of the 江 and has two teats.

shuowen:7606.text: A fish's name, found in 潘 country in 樂浪. Formed from 魚, with abbreviated 沙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7607.text: A fish's name, found in 潘 country in 樂浪. Formed from 魚, with 樂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7608.text: A fish's name, found in 貉 country. Formed from 魚, with abbreviated 羴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7609.text: A fish's name, with patterned skin, found in 東暆, 樂浪. In the fourth year of Shenjue it was first caught, collected, and sent to the Office of Artisans. In King Cheng of Zhou's time, 揚州 presented 鰅. Formed from 魚, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7610.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 庸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7611.text: 烏鰂, a fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 則 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7612.text: The name of a sea fish. Formed from 魚, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7613.text: The name of a sea fish. Formed from 魚, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7614.text: The name of a sea fish. Formed from 魚, with 复 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7615.text: A sea fish whose skin can adorn a sword. Formed from 魚, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7616.text: A great sea fish. Formed from 魚, with 畺 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'Take its 䲔鯢, the great ones.'

shuowen:7617.text: A fish bone. Formed from 魚, with 更 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7618.text: A fish's armor or scales. Formed from 魚, with 粦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7619.text: A fishy smell. Formed from 魚, with 生 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7620.text: A rank, fishy smell. Formed from 魚, with 喿 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'For the meal, use the rank-smelling fat.'

shuowen:7621.text: A minced-fish sauce, produced in Shu. Formed from 魚, with 旨 indicating the sound. Alternatively, the name of a 鮪 fish.

shuowen:7622.text: Preserved fish. In the south it is called 䰼; in the north, 鮺. Formed from 魚, with abbreviated 差 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7623.text: Preserved fish. Alternatively, large fish are called 鮺 and small fish 䰼. Formed from 魚, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7624.text: Spoiled fish. Formed from 魚, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7625.text: A creature that moves in a continuous, winding course. Formed from 魚, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7626.text: The 魵 creature. Formed from 魚, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7627.text: A large shrimp. Formed from 魚, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7628.text: The creature called 當互. Formed from 魚, with 咎 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7629.text: A large shellfish. Alternatively, fish fat. Formed from 魚, with 亢 indicating the sound. Read like 岡.

shuowen:7630.text: A clam. Formed from 魚, with 丙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7631.text: A clam. Formed from 魚, with 吉 indicating the sound. The Han Statutes stipulate that 會稽 commandery present 鮚𤖕, apparently a clam sauce.

shuowen:7632.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7633.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 瞿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7634.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 侯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7635.text: The ends of bones being brittle, perhaps. Formed from 魚, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7636.text: The teeming appearance expressed by 烝然𩷹𩷹. Formed from 魚, with 卓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7637.text: The lively movement of 鱣 and 鮪 fish, expressed by 鮁鮁. Formed from 魚, with 犮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7638.text: The 鯕 fish, found in 東萊. Formed from 魚, with 夫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7639.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 其 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7640.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 兆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7641.text: A fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 匕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7642.text: Fresh fish of the finest quality. Formed from three 魚. Fish that has not deteriorated.

shuowen:7643.text: The fish with both eyes on one side. Formed from 魚, with 枼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7644.text: 文魮, a fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 比 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7645.text: 文鰩, a fish's name. Formed from 魚, with 䍃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7646.text: Two fish. All characters in this group are formed from 𩺰.

shuowen:7647.text: To catch fish. Formed from 𩺰 and 水.

shuowen:7648.text: The dark bird, the swallow. A pinched mouth, spread wings, and branching tail: a pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 燕.

shuowen:7649.text: Chief of scaled creatures. It can be hidden or visible, fine or huge, short or long; at the spring equinox it ascends to heaven, and at the autumn equinox it submerges in the depths. Formed from 肉 and the flying shape of 飛, with abbreviated 童 indicating the sound. All characters in this group are formed from 龍.

shuowen:7650.text: A dragon. Formed from 龍, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7651.text: A dragon's appearance. Formed from 龍, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7652.text: The projecting ridges on a dragon's back, apparently. Formed from 龍, with 幵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7653.text: A flying dragon. Formed from two 龍. Read like 沓.

shuowen:7654.text: A bird soaring. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 飛.

shuowen:7655.text: Wings. Formed from 飛, with 異 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7656.text: To oppose. Formed from the lower wings, 翄, of 飛, taking their facing away from one another. All characters in this group are formed from 非.

shuowen:7657.text: To separate. Formed from 非, with 己 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7658.text: To bend or fall prostrate. Formed from 非, with 麻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7659.text: To oppose one another. Formed from 非, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7660.text: A prison, used to confine wrongdoers. Formed from 非, with abbreviated 陛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7661.text: To fly swiftly. Formed from 飛 with its feathers, 羽, unseen. All characters in this group are formed from 卂.

shuowen:7662.text: To turn swiftly. Formed from 卂, with abbreviated 營 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7663.text: The dark bird, called 𠃉 in Qi and Lu, taking its own call as its name. A pictograph. All graphs in this category are analyzed as containing 𠃉.

shuowen:7664.text: To pass through. Formed from 𠃉 and 子. 𠃉 is the seasonal bird at whose arrival people pray for children. To obtain a child when it arrives is held auspicious and beautiful. In antiquity a person named 嘉 had the courtesy name 子孔.

shuowen:7665.text: For humans and birds, bearing young is called 乳; for beasts, 産. Formed from 孚 and 𠃉. 𠃉 is the dark bird. The Bright Hall's Monthly Ordinances says: 'On the day the dark bird arrives, sacrifice to the High Matchmaker to pray for children.' Thus 乳 includes 𠃉. Prayers for children must be on its arrival day because it comes at the spring equinox and leaves at the autumn equinox, a seasonal bird opening the time of birth, Emperor Shaohao's official in charge of the equinoxes.

shuowen:7666.text: A bird flying upward and soaring without coming down. Formed from 一, which represents heaven; a pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 不.

shuowen:7667.text: No. Formed from 口 and 不; 不 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:7668.text: A bird flying from high above down to the earth. Formed from 一, which represents earth; a pictograph. 不 goes upward, whereas 至 comes downward. All characters in this group are formed from 至.

shuowen:7669.text: To arrive. Formed from 至, with 刀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7670.text: To arrive. Formed from 至, with 秦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7671.text: Angry and perverse. Formed from 至: having arrived, one retreats again. 遜 means to withdraw. The Book of Zhou says: 'The people of Xia were greedy and perverse.' 𦥊 is read like 摯.

shuowen:7672.text: A viewing tower, square and high. Formed from 至 and 之, with abbreviated 高; the same conception as 室 and 屋.

shuowen:7673.text: To arrive. Formed from two 至.

shuowen:7674.text: A bird upon its nest; a pictograph. When the sun is in the west, birds roost, so it came to serve as 西, 'west.' All characters in this group are formed from 西.

shuowen:7675.text: A surname. Formed from 西, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7676.text: Salty earth of the west. Formed from abbreviated 西, depicting 鹽, salt. There is a 鹵 county in 安定. In the east it is called 㡿, in the west 鹵. All characters in this group are formed from 鹵.

shuowen:7677.text: Salty. Formed from 鹵, with abbreviated 差 indicating the sound. In 河内 it is called 𪉤; people of 沛 pronounce it like 虘.

shuowen:7678.text: That which is held in the mouth; the flavor associated with the north. Formed from 鹵, with 咸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7679.text: Salty. Formed from 鹵, with 監 indicating the sound. In antiquity 宿沙 first made salt by boiling seawater. All characters in this group are formed from 鹽.

shuowen:7680.text: The salt lake of 河東: fifty-one li long, seven li wide, and one hundred sixteen li around. Formed from abbreviated 鹽, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7681.text: Saline earth. Formed from abbreviated 鹽, with 僉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7682.text: To protect. Half of a double door is called 戶. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 戶.

shuowen:7683.text: A door leaf. Formed from 戶, with 非 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7684.text: A door leaf. Formed from 戶, with 翄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7685.text: A room at the side. Formed from 戶, with 方 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7686.text: A sliding side door of a covered carriage. Formed from 戶, with 大 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 釱.

shuowen:7687.text: Narrow or constrained. Formed from 戶, with 乙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7688.text: To begin opening. Formed from 戶 and 聿.

shuowen:7689.text: The space between door and window is called 扆. Formed from 戶, with 衣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7690.text: To close. Formed from 戶, with abbreviated 劫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7691.text: A bar that closes a door from outside. Formed from 戶, with 冋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7692.text: To hear, by a sound gloss. Formed from two 戶; a pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 門.

shuowen:7693.text: Heaven's gate. Formed from 門, with 昌 indicating the sound. People of Chu call a gate 閶闔.

shuowen:7694.text: A gate within a palace. Formed from 門, with 韋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7695.text: 䦲 is called 樀; 樀 is a temple gate. Formed from 門, with 詹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7696.text: A lane gate. Formed from 門, with 厷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7697.text: A freestanding door, round above and square below, resembling a 圭 tablet. Formed from 門, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7698.text: A small door beside a gate. Formed from 門, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7699.text: An upper-story door. Formed from 門, with 𦐇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:7700.text: A gate. Formed from 門, with 干 indicating the sound. In 平輿, 汝南, a village gate is called 閈.
